items.title: Section: Freedom From Obstruction Opens — Internal and External Hindrances

items.zh: 云何無障？謂此無障略有二種。一者、依內，二者、依外。我當先說依內外障，與彼相違，當知即是二種無障。
items.en: What is freedom from obstruction? Briefly, this freedom is of two kinds: that which depends on internal factors, and that which depends on external factors. I shall first describe the internal and external obstructions themselves; understand that freedom from them, in each case, is simply their opposite.

items.title: The First Internal Obstacle: Lacking Basic Provisions

items.zh: 云何名依內障？謂如有一，於其先世不曾修福；不修福故，不能時時獲得隨順資生眾具，所謂衣、食、諸坐臥具、病緣醫藥、及餘什具。
items.en: What is meant by an obstacle depending on internal factors? It means that one who, in a former life, never cultivated merit, is consequently unable, from time to time, to obtain the necessities that sustain life — namely, clothing, food, bedding, medicine for illness, and other requisites.

items.title: The Remaining Obstacles to Effort: Affliction, Illness, Imbalance, Undigested Food

items.zh: 有猛利貪及長時貪，有猛利瞋及長時瞋，有猛利癡及長時癡。或於先世積集造作多疾病業。由彼為因，多諸疾病。或由現在行不平等。由是因緣，風熱痰癊、數數發動。或有宿食住在身中。
items.en: There is fierce and prolonged desire, fierce and prolonged aversion, fierce and prolonged delusion. Or one may have accumulated, in a former life, actions that bring about frequent illness — through that cause, illness now frequently arises. Or one may, in the present, live without balance — through that cause, disorders of wind, heat, phlegm, and yin (癊) frequently arise. Or undigested food may remain lodged within the body.

items.title: Section: Ten Obstacles to Genuine Seclusion

items.zh: 或食麁重，多事、多業、多有所作、多與眾會。樂著事業、樂著語言、樂著睡眠、樂著諠眾、樂相雜住、樂著戲論。
items.en: One may eat heavily, be occupied with many affairs, many established enterprises, many tasks, and much socializing. One may delight in busy activity, delight in talk, delight in sleep, delight in noisy crowds, delight in mixed company, and delight in idle speculation.

items.title: Section: Obstacles to Stillness Close Internal Obstruction; Bad Company Opens the External

items.zh: 樂自舉恃、掉亂、放逸、居止非處。如是等類，應知一切名依內障。云何名依外障？謂如有一，依不善士；由彼因緣，不能時時獲得隨順教授教誡。
items.en: One may delight in self-conceit, be restless and scattered, be heedless, or dwell in an unsuitable place. All such things should be understood as obstacles depending on internal factors. What is meant by an obstacle depending on external factors? It means that one who relies on an unwholesome companion is, through that cause, unable to obtain, from time to time, the guidance and correction one needs.

items.title: Section: An Unsuitable Environment Closes External Obstruction Entirely

items.zh: 或居惡處。於此住處，若晝日分，多有種種諠雜、眾集、諸變異事；若於夜分，多有種種高聲、大聲、大眾諠雜；復有種種猛利辛楚風日惡觸；或有種種人及非人怖畏驚恐。如是等類，應知一切名依外障。
items.en: Or one may dwell in an unsuitable place. In such a dwelling, during the day, there may be much noise, crowding, and disruptive commotion; at night, much loud and clamorous noise, large crowds in an uproar; there may also be harsh, punishing wind and sun; or there may be various threats and terrors from human beings and non-human beings alike. All such things should be understood as obstacles depending on external factors.

items.zh: 如是廣辯內外障已。復云何知此中略義？

items.title: Section: The Brief Summary Regroups Everything Into Three Obstacles

items.zh: 謂於此中略有三障。一、加行障，二、遠離障，三、寂靜障。云何加行障？謂若此障會遇現前，於諸善品所有加行皆無堪能，亦無勢力。此復云何？謂常疹疾、困苦、重病，風熱痰癊數數發動，或有宿食住在身中，或被蛇蠍、百足、蚰蜒之所䖧螫，或人非人之所逼惱，又不能得衣、食、臥具、病緣醫藥及餘什具。如是等類，應知一切名加行障。
items.en: Briefly, there are three obstacles here: the obstacle to effort, the obstacle to seclusion, and the obstacle to stillness. What is the obstacle to effort? It means that when this obstacle is actually present, one has no capability at all — no strength — for any wholesome effort. … Namely: constant ailments, or serious illness that brings distress; recurring disorders of wind, heat, phlegm, and yin (癊); undigested food lodged in the body; being stung or bitten by snakes, scorpions, centipedes, or house centipedes; being harassed by human or non-human beings; or being unable to obtain clothing, food, bedding, medicine, or other necessities. All such things should be understood as the obstacle to effort.

items.title: Section: The Obstacle to Seclusion, Unpacked in Far Greater Depth

items.zh: 云何遠離障？謂食麁重。多事、多業、多有所作。或樂事業。由此因緣，愛樂種種所作事業，彼彼事中其心流散。或樂語言。由此因緣，雖於遠離斷寂靜修，有所堪能、有大勢力，然唯讀誦便生喜足。或樂睡眠。由此因緣，惛沈睡眠常所纏繞，為性懈怠，執睡為樂、執倚為樂、執臥為樂。或樂諠眾。由此因緣，樂與在家及出家眾、談說種種王論、賊論、食論、飲論、妙衣服論、婬女巷論、諸國土論、大人傳論、世間傳論、大海傳論。如是等類能引無義虛綺論中，樂共談說，抂度時日。又多愛樂數與眾會。彼彼事中令心散動、令心擾亂。或樂雜住。由此因緣，諸在家眾及出家眾，若未會遇，思慕欲見；若已會遇，不欲別離。或樂戲論。由此因緣，樂著世間種種戲論。於應趣向好樂前行，於遠離中喜捨善軛。如是等類眾多障法，應知一切名遠離障。
items.en: What is the obstacle to seclusion? It is eating heavily, being occupied with many affairs, many established enterprises, many tasks. Or delighting in busy activity. … Or delighting in talk. … Or delighting in sleep. … Or delighting in noisy crowds — through this cause, delighting in discussing with householders and renunciants alike various talk of kings, of thieves, of food, of drink, of fine clothing, of the courtesans' quarter, of foreign lands, of famous people, of worldly gossip, of maritime adventure. Or delighting greatly in frequent socializing. … Or delighting in mixed company. … Or delighting in idle speculation. … All such many obstructive things should be understood as the obstacle to seclusion.

items.zh: 若有此障會遇現前，難可捨離阿練若處、山林、曠野、邊際臥具所有貪著，亦不能居阿練若處、塚間、樹下、空閑靜室。

items.title: Section: The Obstacle to Stillness Opens — Calming's Obstacle in Depth

items.zh: 云何寂靜障？謂寂靜者，即奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。有奢摩他障、有毘鉢舍那障。云何奢摩他障？謂諸放逸及住非處。由放逸故，或惛沈睡眠纏繞其心，或唯得奢摩他便生愛味，或於下劣性心樂趣入，或於闇昧性其心樂著。由住如是非處所故，人或非人諠雜擾亂，他所逼惱，心外馳散。如是名為奢摩他障。當知此障能障寂靜。
items.en: What is the obstacle to stillness? Stillness means calming and insight; there is an obstacle to calming, and an obstacle to insight. What is the obstacle to calming? It is heedlessness and dwelling in an unsuitable place. Through heedlessness, the mind may be bound up in sloth and torpor; or, having attained calming alone, one may become attached to its flavour; or the mind may delight in turning towards base and inferior things; or the mind may become attached to a state of dullness. And because one dwells in such an unsuitable place, one is disturbed by the clamour of humans or non-humans, harassed by them, the mind scattering outward. This is called the obstacle to calming. Know that this obstacle obstructs stillness.

blocks.text: The obstacles to practise, inner and outer, then a regrouping into three. Several of these will sound familiar from Days 169–170; here they are organised differently.
"Freedom from obstruction is of two kinds: depending on internal factors, and depending on external factors." Freedom is simply the absence of the obstacles described.

One who "never cultivated merit in a former life" cannot obtain the necessities. Master Cháng Bǎi: even rejoicing in others' good deeds is merit. Then: "fierce and prolonged desire, aversion, delusion"; frequent illness from past actions; imbalance of the elements; eating before digestion. Then the obstacles to seclusion: eating heavily, many affairs, delight in talk, sleep, crowds. Then conceit, restlessness, heedlessness, an unsuitable place.
Bad companions, through whom "one cannot obtain the guidance and correction one needs"; and an unsuitable environment: noisy by day, clamorous at night, harsh wind and sun, dangers.
Regrouped: obstacles to **effort**, to **seclusion**, to **stillness**. Venerable Miào Jìng: a light illness doesn't matter, but a serious one makes practice impossible.

"Stillness means calming and insight." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Who can cut off afflictions? Only calming and insight; recitation alone won't do." The obstacles to calm are heedlessness and an unsuitable place. Through heedlessness, "having attained calm alone, one may become attached to its flavour".

quiz.q: What two kinds of freedom from obstruction does the treatise name, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi define them?
options: internal and external; internal arises from one's own body and karmic result, external from outside people and events
quiz.why: "Briefly, this freedom is of two kinds: that which depends on internal factors, and that which depends on external factors." Master Cháng Bǎi: internal obstacles depend on one's own body, arising from the karmic result; external ones depend on outer people and events, arising from outer conditions.

quiz.q: What is the first internal obstacle, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng say one cultivates merit in the mind?
options: never cultivating merit in past lives, so one cannot obtain necessities; in the mind, wishing others well, at ease and healthy
quiz.why: "One who, in a former life, never cultivated merit, is consequently unable, from time to time, to obtain the necessities that sustain life." Venerable Miào Jìng: cultivating merit in the mind is wishing everyone well — at ease, healthy, free of illness.

quiz.q: How does one cultivate merit to counter this obstacle, and what does each master add?
options: Miào Jìng speaks of merit in body, speech, and mind; Cháng Bǎi says rejoicing in others' good deeds earns the same merit
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng treats merit through body, speech, and mind — in the mind, wishing others well. Master Cháng Bǎi: rejoicing — even without doing it oneself, rejoicing in others' good deeds brings the same merit.

quiz.q: What are the first obstacles to seclusion, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi count ten?
options: eating heavily, many affairs and undertakings, many tasks …; eating heavily first, affairs and undertakings second, tasks third
quiz.why: "One may eat heavily, be occupied with many affairs, many undertakings, many tasks, and much socializing." Master Cháng Bǎi: eating heavily is the first obstacle to seclusion; many affairs and undertakings the second; many tasks the third.

quiz.q: One external obstacle is relying on an unwholesome companion. How does Master Cháng Bǎi define one?
options: those who undermine right view, conduct, and livelihood, love commotion, are lazy, cling to saṃsāra, turn from awakening, and love household ties
quiz.why: "One who relies on an unwholesome companion is, through that cause, unable to obtain, from time to time, the guidance and correction one needs." Master Cháng Bǎi: anyone who undermines right view, right conduct, or right livelihood, loves commotion, is lazy, clings to birth and death, turns away from awakening, or loves household life is an unwholesome companion.

quiz.q: What does "stillness" refer to, and why does Venerable Miào Jìng say recitation alone is not enough?
options: calming and insight; only these two cut off afflictions — recitation lacks that power
a quiet room; recitation is noisy
quiz.why: "Stillness means calming and insight." Venerable Miào Jìng: who can cut off afflictions? Only calming and insight; recitation alone won't do — it lacks that power.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng comment on "having attained calming alone, one becomes attached to its flavour"?
options: one would expect praise for attaining concentration, but here, not cultivating insight is called heedlessness
quiz.why: "Through heedlessness … having attained calming alone, one may become attached to its flavour." Venerable Miào Jìng: we would think one who attains concentration deserves praise, but here it says that not cultivating insight is heedlessness.
